$comment: Shared vectors of identifier equality (DEC-0076, docs/specification/identifiers.md). A port runs its own normal-form function over `normal` (input → expected) and its own sameness over `same` and `different`. `laxPorts` are the mistakes a lax port makes: `wrong` is what it returns, `expected` the normal form. `schema` is the verdict of `common.schema.json#/$defs/uri` on the input, so a port can check that only a string the schema admits is normalized. The normal form follows RFC 3986 §6.2.2 and, for `urn:`, RFC 8141 §3.1 (both pinned in docs/evidence/sources.md).

normal.name: the scheme is lower-cased
a path keeps its case
a URN's scheme and NID are lower-cased (RFC 8141 §3.1 items 1, 2)
a URN's NSS keeps its case
a URN's percent hex is upper-cased (RFC 8141 §3.1 item 3)
a URN's percent-encoded unreserved character is not decoded (RFC 8141 §3.1)
a URN's r-, q- and f-components are ignored (RFC 8141 §3.1)
a URN's '?' not followed by '+' or '=' is kept
a URN's '/' is part of the NSS
the host is lower-cased, the user information is not
percent hex is upper-cased (RFC 3986 §6.2.2.1)
a percent-encoded unreserved character is decoded (RFC 3986 §6.2.2.2)
a percent-encoded reserved character is not decoded
dot segments are removed (RFC 3986 §6.2.2.3, §5.2.4)
percent-encoded dots are dot segments once decoded
a trailing dot segment leaves the path ending in '/'
a rootless path loses its leading './' (RFC 3986 §5.2.4 step A)
a rootless path loses its leading '../' and './' segments
a rootless path keeps its dot segments further in (the contract's own narrowing, RFC 3986 §6.1)
a rootless path keeps a leading dot segment that would leave it empty
a rootless path keeps a leading dot segment that would leave it absolute
no default port is removed and no empty path becomes '/' (no RFC 3986 §6.2.3)
an IPv6 literal is lower-cased
query and fragment: hex upper-cased, unreserved decoded
an empty string is compared as it is
a string with no scheme is compared as it is
a string with a space is compared as it is
a malformed percent triplet is compared as it is
a port that is not digits is compared as it is
normal.note: RFC 3986 refuses it; the schema's validator (Ajv's `uri` format) admits it, reading `/` and an empty authority before the path `/h:abc/`. Not normalized: a false negative, never a false positive.

normal.name: a URI with neither an authority nor a path is compared as it is
an IP literal that is not one is compared as it is
__proto__ is compared as it is
constructor is compared as it is

laxPorts.name: decoding an unreserved character in a URN's NSS
